1. Stem truncation is the strongest systems lever, and the gain is driven by memory bandwidth. Evidence:
- E028: backward truncation saved about 27% of a 32 px step for about 20% of conv MACs.
- E036: the whitening detach saved 2.4%, more than I predicted.
- E037: the 60% freeze saved another 4.6%.
The large-map work (whitening output at 31×31 with 24 channels, group-1 conv1 dgrad and wgrad, GELU backward) is traffic-bound, not MAC-bound. Group-1 BN runs after the pool, at 15×15, so folding it (I057) attacks the small part of the stem. Bandwidth-bound savings may be smaller on the PCIe judge.

2. The freeze dose has a cliff. Freezing at 75% is about free. Freezing at 60% (E037) cost about 0.4 pp, more than the epoch-dial rate. A mechanism nobody has stated: group 1 must adapt to the 28→32 distribution shift. With the 32 px phase starting at 70%, a freeze at 60% locks group-1 features tuned to 28 px statistics. My inference is that the freeze point should track the start of the last resolution phase (freeze no earlier than about 5% after the switch), not a fixed fraction. forecasts.reason: With no recipe change, seeds 0–2 should repeat the tip's result. Fresh seeds likely put the pooled 20-seed mean below 0.753 because of the winner's curse from gating on seeds 3–12.
Group-1 BN runs after the pool at 15×15, so folding it saves well under 2%. Switching from batch statistics to fixed statistics mid-run also perturbs the downstream groups.
This diagnostic makes no recipe change. I expect the profile to show non-GEMM kernels at 30% or more of GPU time and the stem's share above its MAC share, as E028, E036 and E037 suggest.
Muon is likely worth about 0.4–0.8 pp on a run of about 230 steps at batch 2000. SGD at this batch size is under-tuned, and removing the NS step saves only about 2–3%.

cruxes: Does the safe freeze point track the start of the last resolution phase (group 1 must adapt to the 32 px statistics)? Test: move the 32 px switch to 60% and the freeze to 65%, and check whether E037's loss disappears.
What is the tip's true population mean on fresh seeds? If it is below 0.753, every time lever must also pay for an epoch top-up of about 0.1–0.15 s.
Do the bandwidth-bound stem savings measured on the SXM4 card shrink on the PCIe judge, and does that change which levers are worth keeping?
